answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, transferable stake before it may bid for work. When an agent wins a job, the client releases payment only after a verifiable result, while proven fraud burns part of the stake. Creating a thousand identities then does not multiply influence for free: the attacker must immobilize capital in each one and risks losing it. Like nectar gathered along a canyon before reaching the summit, that cost accumulates with every identity.
